'''Dan-Virgil Voiculescu''' ({{IPA|ro|dan virˈd͡ʒil vojkuˈlesku}}; born 14 June 1949) is a [[Romanians|Romanian]] professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He has worked in single [[operator theory]], operator [[K-theory]] and [[von Neumann algebra]]s. More recently, he developed [[free probability]] theory.

==Education and career==
Voiculescu studied at the [[University of Bucharest]], receiving his PhD in 1977 under the direction of [[Ciprian Foias]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=32920}}</ref> He was an assistant at the University of Bucharest (1972&ndash;1973), a researcher at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]] (1973&ndash;1975), and a researcher at [[INCREST]] (1975&ndash;1986). He came to Berkeley in 1986 for the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], and stayed on as visiting professor. Voiculescu was appointed professor at Berkeley in 1987.

==Awards and honors==
He received the 2004 [[NAS Award in Mathematics]] from the National Academy of Sciences (NAS) for “the theory of free probability, in particular, using [[random matrix|random matrices]] and a new concept of [[entropy]] to solve several hitherto intractable problems in von Neumann algebras.”<ref>Allyn Jackson, [https://www.ams.org/notices/200405/comm-nas.pdf Voiculescu Receives NAS Award in Mathematics], ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]'', May 2004, p. 547.</ref>

Voiculescu was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2006. In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-08-29.</ref>
